title: For representable morphisms the valuative criterion of algebraic spaces is the valuative criterion of schemes
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, the existence part of the valuative criterion in the sense of algebraic spaces is equivalent to the same condition for the solid diagrams with a valuation ring A and fraction field K in the sense of schemes (source lines 8386-8406). The proof shows that the general K' diagram can be pushed down: since f is representable, X_A = Spec(A) x_Y X is a scheme, the morphism Spec(A') -> X gives a point x of X_A, and from the ring diagram with A' dominating A one gets K intersect A' = A, so the image of O_{X_A, x} -> K lies in A and defines the required morphism Spec(A) -> X_A.
